body:
Checked the two new script/package rules against realistic commands, using the regexes exactly as written in the diff. Two things worth tightening before review.

**1. Stray file.** `dangerouspatternspkginstallscriptexec.patch` is committed at the repo root; it is a dump of this same diff. Probably not meant to ship.

**2. False positives from the two new script-execution rules.**

```
FLAG ./scripts/run_tests.sh              (relative-path)
FLAG ./venv/bin/python -m pytest ...     (relative-path)
FLAG ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run      (relative-path)
FLAG pip install -e .                    (pip-install)
FLAG pip install --upgrade pip           (pip-install)
FLAG bash tests/gateway/run_smoke.sh     (script-file)
ok   pip install -r requirements.txt
ok   npm install
```

`./scripts/run_tests.sh` is this repos documented test entry point (root AGENTS.md says to always use `scripts/run_tests.sh`), and `./venv/bin/python` / `./node_modules/.bin/*` are the normal venv and node invocations. Any bare `./` prefix becoming an approval prompt would hit routine work on nearly every checkout. `pip install -e .` (editable dev install) and `pip install --upgrade pip` are the same class.

Suggestion: for the relative-path rule, require a download-ish target rather than any `./` path (e.g. only under a temp dir, or a file that a preceding `curl`/`wget`/`write_file` call produced). For the pip rule, exempt local-path installs (`-e`, `--upgrade pip`, or a path that exists in the tree). The `pip install -r` exclusion and the `npm i -g` / `pipx` / `uv tool` scoping look right as written.

On the design: flagging the execution side (`bash x.sh`, `./x.sh`) instead of tracking downloads across calls is the right call, since it needs no cross-call state. Worth stating that tradeoff in the PR body explicitly, because the download-tracking alternative will come up in review.

Also note `python -m pip install <pkg>` and `uv add` are not covered by the pip rule, if you want the install class to be complete.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

Related: #4502 (open) already adds download-and-execute and supply-chain install patterns to the dangerous-command list, so these two PRs overlap for reviewers to reconcile. Also worth a look: gating every bare `pip install <pkg>` (not just global/tool installs) will prompt on routine project work.

Good catch on both. Fixed the pip false positives (-e ./--editable ., --target ., --upgrade pip/-U pip all exempted now, while a remote -e/--target still flags). Dropped the script-execution patterns entirely — you're right that it's not solvable with a stateless per-command regex, and it false-positived on this repo's own scripts/run_tests.sh. Kept only the pip/npm/pipx/uv-tool half here. One correction: python -m pip install <pkg> is actually already caught — \bpip3?\s+install\b matches "pip install" as a substring regardless of what precedes it; added a test for that. uv add is intentionally not covered — it's project-scoped (writes to pyproject.toml), same category as npm install <pkg> without -g.

On #4502: checked the diff directly. The script-execution overlap is real, hence dropped above. On package installs though, the two aren't covering the same thing — #4502 only flags installs from a suspicious source (arbitrary URL, custom/extra index; pip install requests is explicitly tested as NOT flagged there). This PR flags any global/system install regardless of source, because the incident behind it (installing a legitimate PyPI package, agent-reach) wasn't a malicious-source problem — it was an unauthorized-capability-expansion problem. Complementary policies, not duplicate coverage — happy for maintainers to pick one or merge both.

Independent verification on the PR head (c992aae0): the test file passes locally, 23/23 (canonical runner). I also probed the live matcher directly: pip/python -m pip/uv pip/pipx/uv tool/npm i -g all flag, while -r requirements, -e ., local npm install, and pip self-upgrade stay silent. Case-insensitivity holds via the shared compile flags.

Two residual notes:

1. Real bypass: npm accepts flags before the subcommand, so npm -g install vercel misses (the pattern requires install-then--global). Same class likely applies to npm --global add. One alternation covering both orders closes it.

2. pip install -e ./sub (local-path editable) flags. Conservative direction for a security gate and only costs an approval prompt, but the comment's local-project carve-out reads like it covers this. Either widen the -e/--target exclusion to ./ paths or say remote-only in the comment.
